#### 1. epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to plakophilin deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.443)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6809371, Reactome:R-HSA-6805567, Reactome:R-HSA-6798695)

**Proposed mechanism:** KRT1 (HGNC:6424) —DISRUPTS→ keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0030244); PKP1 (HGNC:9576) —DISRUPTS→ keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0030244); keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0030244) —LEADS_TO→ keratinocyte differentiation (GO:0048755); KRT1 (HGNC:6424) —LEADS_TO→ Palmoplantar keratoderma (HP:0000957); PKP1 (HGNC:9576) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermolysis bullosa simplex (HP:0007300). Mutations in KRT1 disrupt keratin intermediate filament organization, leading to palmoplantar keratoderma. Mutations in PKP1 also disrupt keratin intermediate filament organization by affecting desmosome integrity and cell-cell adhesion, contributing to epidermolysis bullosa simplex. Both pathways converge on the keratin intermediate filament network, impacting keratinocyte differentiation and integrity.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with mutations in KRT1 or PKP1 that result in completely normal skin phenotype, or demonstration that the keratin intermediate filament organization pathway is not affected in either disease. _(variant: The presence of common pathogenic variants in KRT1 or PKP1 in the gnomAD database with frequencies exceeding 0.1% would cast doubt on their exclusive role in these rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on keratin intermediate filament organization and keratinocyte differentiation provides a potential therapeutic avenue. Modulating pathways that stabilize keratin networks or enhance keratinocyte cohesion could offer benefit for both conditions, despite their distinct clinical presentations.
